goals: Integrate the accepted-for-review controller EvidenceBundle core from the continuation base into the Supervisor CLI without changing RunManifest task authority. In src/supervisor/cli.ts, generate the final evidence bundle after the Worker batch returns terminal path, cleanup, boundary and cost facts; expose a bounded evidence status projection and supervisor evidence command that reads or regenerates .cliyard/evidence/<runId>.json. A completed-run resume must repair a missing bundle before returning. Missing or invalid evidence must be degraded, never success. Add tests/supervisor-evidence-bundle.test.ts and update tests/supervisor-cli.test.ts to cover completed and blocked runs, automatic creation, status JSON/human output, invalid or missing evidence, explicit regeneration without RunManifest mutation, completed resume repair, exact path/process/boundary/cost inclusion and running-manifest rejection. Preserve existing commands and behavior. Do not modify evidence-bundle.ts or any eval files.
nonGoals: Do not modify the EvidenceBundle core or run schema.
Do not mutate task verdicts or acceptance.
deliverables: Automatic final EvidenceBundle generation for terminal runs.
Read-only degraded status and explicit evidence regeneration.
Completed-run evidence repair and integration tests.
forbidden: Do not rewrite a RunManifest to claim evidence exists.

goals: Integrate the accepted-for-review Harness Eval core from the continuation base into the CLI and add the deterministic scenario suite. Add src/evaluation/cli.ts, src/evaluation/scenarios.ts and src/evaluation/handoff.ts, wire src/cli.ts and package.json, and add examples/harness-eval/suite.json. Implement cliyard eval run --suite <path> --label <id> --repetitions <n> --out <dir> --json and eval compare --baseline <run.json> --candidate <run.json> --out <path> --json. Execute argv arrays without a shell, with fixed cwd, bounded output/timeouts, exact clean commit binding and fail-closed paths. Define six scenarios: normal-work, high-fanout-process-tree, verifier-timeout-and-extension, controller-sigkill-recovery, path-escape and context-reload-handoff. Reuse real existing focused tests where appropriate. Add tests/harness-eval-cli.test.ts and tests/harness-eval-handoff.test.ts; the handoff test must start a fresh process that reads only a terminal RunManifest/EvidenceBundle fixture and reconstructs the next action. Cover malformed suites/outputs, expected nonzero, timeout, repetition failure, unavailable metrics, flips, unsafe ids/paths and secret-free bounds. Do not modify eval core files, Supervisor or add paid provider calls.
nonGoals: Do not modify the accepted-for-review eval core.
Do not call paid models or add an LLM judge.
Do not add daemon, routing or admission.
verifyCommands: npm run harness-eval -- run --suite examples/harness-eval/suite.json --label smoke --repetitions 1 --out .cliyard/evals/smoke --json
deliverables: Working eval run/compare CLI and package script.
Six bounded local scenarios with fresh-process handoff reconstruction.
Deterministic JSON/Markdown reports with flips and explicit missing metrics.
forbidden: Do not use a shell to execute scenario commands.
Do not treat missing provider metrics as zero.
Do not add paid eval calls.

goals: Run the accepted Harness Eval v0 CLI twice at this exact continuation base with at least two repetitions per scenario, compare the baseline and candidate reports, and add docs/evidence/HARNESS_EVAL_V0.md with only observed facts. Record repetition-level outcomes, scenario flips, durations, the known deadline-extension flake if it appears, missing request/token/cache/cost/human-intervention metrics, exact commands, base commit, report paths and final focused/build/full results. Record how a fresh process reconstructs the next action from an EvidenceBundle handoff fixture. Clearly state that baseline and candidate are same-commit repeatability checks, not a Harness improvement or paid-model quality claim. Do not modify source, tests, Plan or contracts.
nonGoals: Do not edit implementation or tests.
Do not claim an improvement from same-code runs.
Do not hide repetition failures behind aggregate pass rate.
